# Load prerequisite

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)
library(here)
library(ggstatsplot)
library(ggplot2)
library(hrbrthemes)
library(ggh4x)

monthly13_pairs <- read_csv(here("00_data", "processed", "lst_cooling_pairs_monthly_1330.csv"))

monthly01_pairs <- read_csv(here("00_data", "processed", "lst_cooling_pairs_monthly_0130.csv"))


# filter to include only the hottest months (based on monthly air temp)
hottest_month_tair_01 <- monthly01_pairs |>
  filter(
    (year == 2021 & month == 3) |
    (year == 2022 & month == 2) |
    (year == 2023 & month == 2) |
    (year == 2024 & month == 3)
  ) |>
  mutate(year = factor(year))

hottest_month_tair_13 <- monthly13_pairs |>
  filter(
    (year == 2021 & month == 3) |
    (year == 2022 & month == 2) |
    (year == 2023 & month == 2) |
    (year == 2024 & month == 3)
  ) |>
  mutate(year = factor(year))


```

```{r}
# test for normality --> no evidence against normal destribution
years <- c(2021, 2022, 2023, 2024)

for (yr in years) {
  
  x <- hottest_month_tair_01 %>%
    filter(year == yr) %>%
    pull(cooling)
  
  cat("\nYear:", yr, "\n")
  print(shapiro.test(x))
}

#check min and max cooling for each year
hottest_month_tair_01 %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    min_cooling = round(min(cooling, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    max_cooling = round(max(cooling, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    mean_cooling = round(mean(cooling, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    sd_cooling = round(sd(cooling, na.rm = TRUE), 2)
  )

hottest_month_tair_01 %>%
  filter(year %in% c(2021, 2022, 2023)) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    min_cooling = min(cooling, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_cooling = max(cooling, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_cooling = mean(cooling, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_cooling = sd(cooling, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_min = round(mean(min_cooling), 2),
    avg_max = round(mean(max_cooling), 2),
    avg_mean = round(mean(mean_cooling), 2),
    avg_sd = round(mean(sd_cooling), 2)
  )


```

### Hypothesis (important)

Because you *expect 2024 \> 2021*, this is a **one-sided paired test**.

**Null hypothesis (H₀):**

H0: μ2024−μ2021=0

(no change in cooling )

**Alternative hypothesis (H₁):**

H1: μ2024−μ2021\>0

(2024 is warmer on average)

#### Compare El Nino year (2024) to all reference years (2021, 2022, 2023)

```{r}

df = df13_wide

# library(tidyverse)
# Run the paired t-test in R
test1 <- t.test(df$`2024`, df$`2021`,
       paired = TRUE,
       alternative = "greater")

# Run the paired t-test in R
test2 <- t.test(df$`2024`, df$`2022`,
       paired = TRUE,
       alternative = "greater")

# Run the paired t-test in R
test3 <- t.test(df$`2024`, df$`2023`,
       paired = TRUE,
       alternative = "greater")
test1
test2
test3
# Bind the p values all together to perform multiple testing
p <- c(test1$p.value, test2$p.value, test3$p.value)
test1$p.value
test2$p.value
test3$p.value

# perform multiple testing with Bonferony Holm
p.adjust(p, method = "holm", n = length(p))
```

#### Compare all reference years (2021, 2022, 2023) among each other

```{r}
# test and plot the difference between the reference years
df_cool_reference_years <- hottest_month_tair_13 |>
  filter(
    (year == 2021) |
    (year == 2022) |
    (year == 2023)
#     (year == 2024 & month == 4)
  )

# Welch's one-way ANOVA
oneway.test(
  cooling ~ year,
  data =df_cool_reference_years,
  var.equal = FALSE
)



```

# Plot elevations

```{r}

plot_cooling_vs_elevation <- function(df, method = "lm") {

  # Determine smoothing method and formula
  if (method == "poly") {
    smooth_method <- "lm"
    smooth_formula <- y ~ poly(x, 2)
    plot_title <- "Polynomial model"
  } else {
    smooth_method <- method
    smooth_formula <- NULL
    plot_title <- switch(
      method,
      lm = "Linear model",
      loess = "Loess model",
      gam = "GAM model",
      paste(toupper(method), "model")
    )
  }
  
  # Change here Y to forest, open_land or cooling depending on your needs

  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = elv_mean, y = open_land)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_smooth(
      method = smooth_method,
      formula = smooth_formula,
      color = "red",
      fill = "#69b3a2",
      se = TRUE
    ) +
  # scale_y_continuous( # ----------------> scale for cooling
  #   limits = c(-2, 14),
  #   breaks = seq(-2, 14, by = 2)
  # ) +
    labs(
      x = "Elevation (m)",
      y = "Forest Cooling (°C)",
      title = plot_title
    ) +
    facet_wrap(~year, ncol = 4) +
    theme_ipsum()

  return(p)
}


# Linear
plot_cooling_vs_elevation(hottest_month_tair_13, "lm")

# Polynomial (quadratic)
plot_cooling_vs_elevation(hottest_month_tair_13, "poly")

# Loess
plot_cooling_vs_elevation(hottest_month_tair_13, "loess")

# GAM (if desired)
plot_cooling_vs_elevation(hottest_month_tair_13, "gam")
```

New elevation correlations plots

```{r}


df <- hottest_month_tair_01
# --------------------------------------------------
# 1. Prepare and reshape the data
# --------------------------------------------------

df_13 <- df |>
  dplyr::rename(
    `Elevation (m)` = elv_mean,
    `Forest LST (°C)` = forest,
    `Open-land LST (°C)` = open_land,
    `Forest cooling (°C)` = cooling
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      `Forest LST (°C)`,
      `Open-land LST (°C)`,
      `Forest cooling (°C)`
    ),
    names_to = "response",
    values_to = "value"
  )

# Optional: make sure years appear in the correct order
df_13$year <- factor(
  df_13$year,
  levels = c(2021, 2022, 2023, 2024)
)

# Optional: control row order
df_13$response <- factor(
  df_13$response,
  levels = c(
    "Forest LST (°C)",
    "Open-land LST (°C)",
    "Forest cooling (°C)"
  )
)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 2. Calculate correlation and regression statistics
# --------------------------------------------------

stats_13 <- df_13 |>
  group_by(year, response) |>
  summarise(
    r = cor(
      `Elevation (m)`,
      value,
      use = "complete.obs"
    ),

    b = coef(
      lm(value ~ `Elevation (m)`)
    )[2],
    RSE = sigma(
      lm(value ~ `Elevation (m)`)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# --------------------------------------------------
# 3. Format labels for each panel
# --------------------------------------------------

stats_13 <- stats_13 |>
  mutate(
    label = paste0(
      "r = ", sprintf("%.2f", r),
      "; b = ", sprintf("%.3f", b),
      "\nRSE = ", sprintf("%.2f", RSE)
    )
  )

# Check the statistics
stats_13

# --------------------------------------------------
# 4. Create the figure
# --------------------------------------------------

p13 <- ggplot(
  df_13,
  aes(
    x = `Elevation (m)`,
    y = value
  )
) +

  # Points
  geom_point(
    size = 1.5,
    alpha = 0.9
  ) +

  
geom_smooth(
  method = "loess",
  se = FALSE,
  linewidth = 0.8,
    color = "darkgrey"
) +
  
# One linear regression per panel
geom_smooth(
  method = "lm",
  se = FALSE,
  linewidth = 0.8
) +

# Add r, slope and RSE
geom_text(
  data = stats_13,
  aes(
    x = Inf,
    y = Inf,
    label = label
  ),
  inherit.aes = FALSE,
  hjust = 1.1,
  vjust = 1.3,
  size = 3.2
) +

# Rows = response variables
# Columns = years
facet_grid(
  response ~ year,
  scales = "free_y"
) +
```

```{r}
# Predict from LOESS

  loess_mod,
  newdata = data.frame(elv_mean = x)

# Add fitted curve
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)

get_loess_turning_points <- function(df) {

  mod <- loess(cooling ~ elv_mean, data = df)

  elev_grid <- seq(
    min(df$elv_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(df$elv_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    length.out = 1000
  )

  pred <- predict(
    mod,
    newdata = data.frame(elv_mean = elev_grid)
  )

  # Remove any NA predictions
  tmp <- data.frame(
    elv_mean = elev_grid,
    cooling_fit = pred
  ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(cooling_fit))

  # Change in sign of the fitted slope
  slope_sign <- sign(diff(tmp$cooling_fit))
  turning <- diff(slope_sign)

  max_idx <- which(turning < 0) + 1
  min_idx <- which(turning > 0) + 1

  bind_rows(
    data.frame(
      type = "local_maximum",
      elv_mean = tmp$elv_mean[max_idx],
      fitted_cooling = tmp$cooling_fit[max_idx]
    ),
    data.frame(
      type = "local_minimum",
      elv_mean = tmp$elv_mean[min_idx],
      fitted_cooling = tmp$cooling_fit[min_idx]
    )
  )
}

turning_points <- hottest_month_tair_01 %>%
  filter(year %in% c(2021, 2022, 2023, 2024)) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  group_modify(~ get_loess_turning_points(.x)) %>%
  ungroup() 

turning_points |>
  arrange(type,elv_mean) |>
  group_by(type)|>
  summarize(
    mean_fitted_cooling = round(mean(fitted_cooling),2)
  )
```
